WICKLOW COUNTY COUNCIL ANNOUNCES 95% FUNDING FOR COMMUNITY TREE PLANTING 
Wicklow County Council’s popular Annual Tree Planting Grant Scheme is now accepting applications, 
offering enhanced funding of up to 95% of project costs. This initiative aims to support local biodiversity 
and climate action projects. Community groups have until Sunday, 28th September to apply.  
The scheme provides financial support for Tidy Towns committees, residents associations, schools, 
sports clubs and other community groups to plant native trees, mixed native hedgerows and suitable fruit 
trees in public spaces. This year, applicants can receive up to €500, which covers nearly the entire cost of 
their planting projects.  
The initiative aims to increase tree cover and hedgerows in Wicklow’s towns and villages, aligning with 
the All-Ireland Pollinator Plan and contributing to the Council’s Climate and Biodiversity Action Plans. The 
late autumn and winter months are ideal for planting, as it allows trees to establish strong roots before 
spring growth.

Housing Allocations June & July 2025 
Wicklow County Council successfully allocated over 90 new social homes in June.  Many of these new 
homes became available with the completion of three new estates: Doire Dubh in Tinahely, Cois Droichid 
in Greystones and Tinakilly Park in Rathnew. The three new estates consists of 1 bedroom, 2 bedroom 
and 3 bedroom homes, all of which have an ‘A’ BER rating and are finished to a high standard.  
The three bed units in Tinakilly Park were allocated by Choice Based Letting.  The Choice Based Letting 
is a system which enables Wicklow County Council to allocate some of its’ social housing units, to 
approved social housing applicants by the way of an express of interest. There were 36 social housing 
applicants who expressed their interest in this three bed units. 
This CBL has also utilised for a development of 56 apartments in Altidore Gardens, 
NewtownmountKennedy. These two and three bed apartments will be managed by the Approved 
Housing Body, Co-operative Housing Ireland (CHI). 
A total of 75 social housing applicants expressed their interest in these units. The allocation of these 
units to the successful social housing applicants in Altidore Gardens is nearing completion.

Housing Needs Assessment 2024 (SSHA 2024)

assessments of national housing need. It provides vital data to inform the ongoing development of housing policy.

total number of households qualified for social housing support across the county whose social housing need is not 
being met, in order to understand the level of need for such support. The social housing applications were reviewed

Assessment criteria

Homeless HAP Place Finder 
The Homeless HAP Place finder provides assistance in:  
➢ Seeking out potential properties suitable for households currently identified as homeless or at risk of 
homelessness.  
➢ Liaising with specific households to establish their specific needs.  
➢ Establishing relationships with local property agents and landlords; and,  
➢ Supporting those homeless households to (a) prevent the necessity to enter emergency 
accommodation or (b) to exit emergency accommodation and secure a tenancy.  
➢ To date, 652 households (454 families & 197 singles) have been assisted under the Homeless HAP 
Scheme in Wicklow County Council from the inception on 1st October 2018 to 31st August,2025. (253 
homeless cases, 362 prevention cases to date and 37 direct provision). 165 properties were sourced 
by WCC. 
 
Addressing Homelessness in Partnership with Approved Housing Bodies 
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – Kilmantin Hill, Wicklow 
Kilmantin Hill has 11 rooms to support persons either homeless, exiting a higher support facility, or in danger 
of becoming homeless.  
There are 9 clients supported in the Kilmantin Hill facility, operated by Dublin Simon. There is continuous 
transition by the clients to suitable alternative accommodation. 
A report is being undertaken at present to cost the refurbishment of the current rooms with a view to making 
them all ensuite. More details will be available over the coming months.

Homeless Family Service – Fitzwilliam Road, Wicklow   
Dublin Simon are engaged by Wicklow County Council to operate and manage the facility at Fitzwilliam 
Road, Wicklow as a Family Homeless Service. The building comprises of three 1-bed units, two 2-bed units, 
and two 3-bed units. Eleven families have now transitioned or are in the process of transitioning to a 
permanent home and the resulting vacancies are in the process of being occupied with families 
experiencing or in danger of homelessness. 
It is envisaged that families will avail of the service for circa 6-months STA (Supported Temporary 
Accommodation) with key working support to enable families to transition from homelessness into 
Homeless HAP, or alternative longer-term accommodation.   
Homeless Supported Temporary Accommodation – San Remo, Bray 
San Remo is operated by Dublin Simon and incorporates a service model whereby there are a number of 
emergency/cold weather initiative beds and Supported Temporary Accommodation Beds (STA). There is 
on site key working support linking in with clients.    
The Neighbourhood Liaison Committee is now operational and meets monthly. 
Bi-monthly meetings are held with Dublin Simon and Wicklow County Council staff. 
 
Homeless Supported Accommodation - Carraig Eden, Greystones 
This facility provides 35 ensuite bedrooms with associated kitchens and common areas and is fully 
operational. Wicklow County Council run an in-reach service with the clients to support them as they 
continue their journey into more permanent accommodation.  
 
Other Homeless Supported Accommodation 
Wicklow County Council owned properties in Wicklow, Bray, and Greystones, leased to Approved Housing 
Bodies, provide 12 units of low to medium supported accommodation targeted to the particular support 
needs of the clients. Six of these persons living in shared accommodation have now successfully moved 
into their forever homes and this in turn created space to move further people out of homelessness.  
A homeless outreach service has been rolled out in Bray and is proving very successful.

Action 3.8 Appoint Healthy Age Friendly Homes Co-ordinator & Rollout Wicklow Programme  
Healthy Age Friendly Homes (HAFH) Programme is a support coordination programme that aims to enable 
older people to age in place and reduce the need to transfer to long-term residential care. The Programme 
is a collaboration between the Department of Health and the Department of Housing and Local 
Government. It is funded by the Department of Health and operated by Meath County Council, on behalf of 
all Local Authorities.  
The service is designed to enable older people to remain living in their own home for longer. The local 
coordinator undertakes home visits to older people living in the community, where a needs assessment is 
carried out, looking at four key areas of supports: housing, health, community/social supports, and 
technology. Home visits from the local co-coordinator are available to anyone aged 65+years. The rollout 
of the programme will commence in January 2024. 
Meanwhile referrals for the service can be registered with National Office at 046 924 8899 or via email:

Disability Inclusion Steering Group 
The Sunflower Lanyard Programme aims to easily identify people with hidden disabilities. This Programme 
was rolled out in Wicklow County Council. Members of the Customer Care Unit currently wear these 
Lanyards so that a person with a hidden disability can identify which member of staff they need to talk too. 
Sunflower lanyards are worn by people who have a disability that you might not be able to see. They are 
worn by people who want to let you know that they might need some extra help. 
 
This could be, for example: 
● sensory loss, including difficulty seeing or hearing 
● a physical disability that may not be obvious 
● Autism 
● a learning disability 
● anxiety or any other mental health condition. 
 
There is no qualifying list of hidden disabilities. If a person has a hidden disability and feel that they would 
benefit from wearing a sunflower lanyard, they can in the knowledge that their local community that they 
live in and work in understands this and supports them. 
 
People with hidden disabilities can contribute enormously to their local community and if they feel they are 
supported by their community around them, this can have an immensely positive impact on their lives too. 
 
When Newtown Community Forum Committee launched their campaign, they estimated that less than 10% 
of the community were aware of the existence of the Sunflower Lanyard, let alone what it stood for. Now a 
mere six months later, due to the work of the group and the buy-in from the businesses, community groups 
and the community in general, the Forum estimate that over 90% of the town understand what the Lanyard 
stands for now and would support its users. 
The Sunflower Lanyards are now available in several prominent locations. Should anyone feel they could 
benefit from wearing one. The list of locations are The Post Office, Fishers, Red Eye Coffee, The Parkview 
Hotel, Adrian Dunne Pharmacy, The Pilates Studio, Dunnes Stores, The Primary Care Centre, Newtown 
Area Sports Development, Newtown Primary School, Woodstock Educate Together School, Cali Special 
Class, Eugene`s Food Store and the Wicklow Wolf Taproom.

Spongeworks on Aughrim River 
 
Wicklow County Council in partnership with the Wicklow Uplands Council, the East Wicklow Rivers Trust and 
LAWPRO have been selected to participate in an EU horizon programme called SpongeWorks. After the programme 
received over 70 applications eight regions were chosen to become associated regions in the project which aims to 
help shape how Europe manages water, land, and climate risks.  Each participating region will work on strategy to 
develop and scale sponge measures – Nature based Solutions that help retain water, reduce flood or drought risk 
and restore ecosystems. Wicklow’s project explores restoring the upper Aughrim River’s capacity to slow water flow.

then be scaled up with new tools developed for their implementation and the embedding of sponge strategy into local 
governance and planning.

Croí Cónaithe (Towns, Cities and Rural) – Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant   
The Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant is a payment you can get if you are turning a vacant house or building into 
your permanent home or a rental property.  The grant applies to qualifying vacant properties in cities, towns, villages and 
rural parts of the country. 
There are 2 types of Grants available: 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant of up to €50,000 
• 
Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant including the Derelict Property top up grant of up €70,000 
To qualify for the top up of €20,000, an independent report prepared by a Structural Engineer, along with a copy of their 
Professional Indemnity Insurance, is required to be submitted along with the application, confirming, to the satisfaction of 
the local authority, that the property is derelict i.e. structurally unsound and dangerous. 
To qualify for the grant, applicants must: 
Have proof of ownership or evidence of active negotiations to buy the property (that is, confirmation of engagement from 
the estate agent or owner of the property) where you are seeking approval in principle for a grant. 
- 
Live in the property as your principal private residence or make it available for rent. 
- 
Have proof that the property has been vacant for at least 2 years and that it was built up to and including 2007.
